desc:
Schema markup for products and reviews adds hidden structured data to your pages so search engines can read prices, stock, brand and ratings. Ecom Swift LLC adds the markup to your store, tests it with Google's tools and fixes any warnings.

## What is schema markup?

Schema markup is a block of structured code added to a page that tells search engines exactly what the page contains. On a product page it names the product, its price, whether it is in stock, the brand and the rating from real reviews. Shoppers never see it, but search engines read it.

Without it, search engines must guess these details from the visible text. Guessing works for simple pages and fails for pages with variants, sale prices or unusual layouts.

## Why structured data matters for a store

Online stores are made of facts: a price, a currency, an availability status, a model, a review count. Search engines can display some of these facts in results, but only when they trust that they have read them correctly. Structured data removes the doubt.

It also protects against mismatch. If a result shows one price and the page shows another, shoppers lose trust and search engines may ignore the data. Correct markup, kept in step with the page, avoids that.

## How structured data affects visibility and clicks

When your markup is valid and your pages meet the search engine's rules, results may be shown with extra details such as price, availability or rating. These details make a listing easier to compare and can bring more qualified clicks. The shopper sees what they need before they visit.

We cannot promise that any result will display extras, because search engines decide this themselves and can change their rules. What we can do is make sure your data is correct, complete and eligible, which is the part within your control.

## What a complete schema setup includes

- Product data on every product template.
- Price, currency and stock status that match the visible page.
- Brand, product identifiers and images where your data has them.
- Review rating data pulled from your review app, only when reviews are real and shown on the page.
- Organization data with your name, logo and contact details.
- Breadcrumb data that mirrors your page trail.
- Optional FAQ data on pages that carry real questions and answers.
- Article data for blog posts.
- Local business data when you have a physical shop.
- Testing of sample pages to confirm there are no errors.

## How we add and test it

We first check what your theme and apps already output, since duplicate or conflicting markup is a common fault. We then add or correct the data in your theme or through the platform's own tools, keeping it tied to the information shown on the page.

After that we test sample pages with Google's testing tools, fix errors and warnings, and give you a short record of what was added to which page type.

The Basic package covers product data, with price and stock, tested on sample pages. The Standard package adds review rating data, organization and breadcrumb data and fixes testing warnings. The Premium package adds FAQ, article and local data, checks variants and offers, and sets up Search Console monitoring for enhancements. Add-ons include more sample tests, video data and a later health check.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Keep marked-up prices and stock identical to the visible page.
- Mark up only reviews that real customers wrote and that appear on the page.
- Test after every theme change or app update.
- Use one source of markup, not several overlapping ones.
- Fix warnings as well as errors where practical.

**Avoid:**
- Marking up content that is not on the page.
- Inventing ratings or review counts.
- Leaving old markup from a removed app in the theme.
- Adding FAQ data to pages with no questions.
- Expecting stars to appear in search the day you add data.

## Who this service is for

A store with a review app whose ratings never appear in search can have the connection checked. A seller who changed themes and lost product data will want it restored. A shop that sees structured data errors in Search Console needs them diagnosed.

It also suits stores about to add a blog, FAQ pages or a physical location, where extra data types apply.

## What we need from you

Send your store address and tell us which review app you use, if any. We need access to your theme or settings as a collaborator, staff or developer user, and we never ask for your password. If your platform limits what can be edited, we explain what is possible before starting. A developer is not needed afterward for normal use.
